draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kumarakom! You're on the edge of Vembanad, the biggest lake in Kerala. The bird sanctuary here began as a rubber estate owned by an English planter.
draft.hungryLine: Karimeen pollichathu, pearl spot fish grilled in banana leaf, is the dish to eat here.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Go to the bird sanctuary at sunrise, then drift on Vembanad Lake by country boat.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Take a slow sunset cruise on the lake and watch the fishing canoes come home.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Ask a boatman to take you past Pathiramanal, a small island in the lake whose name means 'midnight sand'.

legends.title: The island that rose at midnight
legends.body: A story says a young Brahmin dove into the lake for his evening prayers, and the waters parted to make an island for him at midnight. That's how Pathiramanal got its name.

legends.title: Baker's estate
legends.body: The bird sanctuary was once Alfred George Baker's rubber plantation. His old bungalow still stands nearby.

tips.title: Birds before 8 am.
tips.body: By mid-morning most of them have gone quiet.

tips.title: Day cruise or overnight?
tips.body: A day cruise gives you the lake for much less.

story.title: A great lake
story.body: Vembanad is fed by several rivers and meets the sea near Kochi. Fishing villages have lived along its edges for centuries.

story.title: A planter's land
story.body: Alfred George Baker, an English planter, reclaimed land here and planted rubber and coconut.

story.title: The sanctuary
story.body: Baker's estate became a bird sanctuary, where herons and migratory birds now nest.

story.title: Houseboats
story.body: Old rice barges called kettuvallam were rebuilt as houseboats, and Kumarakom became one of Kerala's favourite lake escapes.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Birds at sunrise, karimeen for lunch and the lake at sunset. Tell me if you spot a kingfisher.
